A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Boundary Embedding Shaping (BES) work. All 27 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original BES node-classification and link-prediction experiments, component ablations, embedding visualizations, and efficiency measurements in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and convergence analyses.

M1.justification: Boundary selection, the gravity objective and center-based approximation, adaptive parameter updates, attention layers, and decoder remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B–C. Replacing 'determined by parameter' with 'parameterized by' in C.1 is editorial.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same node-classification and link-prediction tasks on WikiCS, Cora, CiteSeer, Pubmed, Chameleon, Cornell, Texas, Roman-empire, ogbn-arxiv, and ogbl-collab. No training or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in each corresponding comparison, including Table 1 and Appendix Tables 9–12. The baseline paragraph is reflowed, but no evaluated GNN, MPNN, NodeImport, MotifRGC, GraphECL, or IGCL comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the non-OGB 60%/20%/20% splits and official OGB protocol. Metrics, training budgets, model configurations, and ablation settings in Appendices C–D are unchanged.

E4.justification: The same neighbor-selection comparison, pairwise-versus-center approximation analysis, component and boundary-node ablations, sensitivity plots, visualizations, and convergence analyses remain. The rewritten Section 5.2 ablation description introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over five runs and retain the same random-seed statement. Standard-deviation reporting in the appendix tables is unchanged; no uncertainty procedure or run-count disclosure is added.

E6.justification: Numerical results, result entries, plotted trends, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains BES WikiCS accuracies of 85.52 for node classification and 92.27 for link prediction.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same latent-variable model, assumptions, block-identifiability definition, theorem, corollary, and error-bound proposition. Their Appendix A proofs, the method derivations, and Appendix B complexity analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about boundary-focused structural disentanglement, controlled parameter updates, theoretical guarantees, and benchmark performance, including the stated average 3.3% GCN improvement.

C2.justification: Explanations of structural-noise filtering, diminishing gains from additional attention layers, and the center approximation retain their meaning. The discussion of relaxed theoretical prerequisites and future low-label or self-supervised extensions is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same implementation equations, dataset descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware, and software versions. Code-access information is unchanged. 'Github' becomes 'GitHub' in Table 3 without changing the implementation source.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged. Section 6 repairs the grammar of the sentence describing existing disentanglement methods, while retaining the same characterization of prior work and BES's positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized copyedits: capitalizing preliminary labels, rewriting the ablation introduction in Section 5.2, repairing a related-work sentence, and tightening Appendix C wording. Terminology and punctuation are standardized without reorganizing the document.

P2.justification: Several table captions replace 'top 1st' with '1st'; Table 1 also receives a punctuation correction. Caption shortening causes small spacing shifts, notably on page 26. Figures, table structures, axes, legends, and numerical contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revised ablation description in Section 5.2, repaired related-work sentence in Section 6, and clearer parameter wording in Appendix C.1 modestly improve readability. Methods, proofs, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited to editorial clarity.
